questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: X is a crystalline sodium salt. Its aqueous solution turns litmus red and releases a gas that makes limewater milky when added to sodium carbonate. With barium chloride solution, X gives a white precipitate insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid. What is X?
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium hydrogensulfate, NaHSO₄, forms an acidic solution. Its hydrogen ions react with carbonate to release CO₂, which makes limewater milky. Its sulfate ions form insoluble white BaSO₄ with barium ions.
questions.explanation: Sodium hydrogensulfate, NaHSO₄, forms an acidic solution. Its hydrogen ions react with carbonate to release CO₂, which makes limewater milky. Its sulfate ions form insoluble white BaSO₄ with barium ions.

questions.question: Sodium chloride may be obtained from brine by
questions.ai_explanation: Evaporation removes water from brine. The dissolved sodium chloride remains and crystallises as enough water is lost.
questions.explanation: Evaporation removes water from brine. The dissolved sodium chloride remains and crystallises as enough water is lost.

questions.question: The alkanol obtained from the production of soap is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
In which of these reactions is iron oxidised?
1. Fe + H₂SO₄ → H₂ + FeSO₄
2. FeSO₄ + H₂S → FeS + H₂SO₄
3. 2FeCl₂ + Cl₂ → 2FeCl₃
4. 2FeCl₃ + SnCl₂ → 2FeCl₂ + SnCl₄
questions.ai_explanation: Oxidation means an increase in oxidation state. Iron changes from 0 to +2 in reaction 1 and from +2 to +3 in reaction 3. It remains +2 in reaction 2 and is reduced from +3 to +2 in reaction 4. Therefore, iron is oxidised in 1 and 3.
questions.explanation: Oxidation means an increase in oxidation state. Iron changes from 0 to +2 in reaction 1 and from +2 to +3 in reaction 3. It remains +2 in reaction 2 and is reduced from +3 to +2 in reaction 4. Therefore, iron is oxidised in 1 and 3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The flame used by welders in cutting metals is
questions.ai_explanation: Burning acetylene in oxygen produces the hot oxy-acetylene flame used for welding and cutting suitable metals. Oxygen alone is not a fuel.
questions.explanation: Burning acetylene in oxygen produces the hot oxy-acetylene flame used for welding and cutting suitable metals. Oxygen alone is not a fuel.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Consecutive members of an alkane homologous series differ by
questions.ai_explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Increasing n by one adds one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms, so successive members differ by CH₂.
questions.explanation: Alkanes have the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Increasing n by one adds one carbon atom and two hydrogen atoms, so successive members differ by CH₂.

questions.question: If an element has the electronic configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p², it is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
An organic compound X has relative molecular mass 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water, containing C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. It has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and absence of air, X forms compound Y and a colourless gas. Y reacts with sodium to release gas Z, which gives a pop with a lighted splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to form a sweet-smelling compound W.

Compound W is
questions.ai_explanation: Yeast converts glucose to ethanol, so Y is ethanol. Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water. Ethyl ethanoate belongs to the ester family, making W an ester.
questions.explanation: Yeast converts glucose to ethanol, so Y is ethanol. Ethanol reacts with ethanoic acid to form ethyl ethanoate and water. Ethyl ethanoate belongs to the ester family, making W an ester.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
An organic compound X has relative molecular mass 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water, containing C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. It has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and absence of air, X forms compound Y and a colourless gas. Y reacts with sodium to release gas Z, which gives a pop with a lighted splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to form a sweet-smelling compound W.

The molecular formula of X is
questions.ai_explanation: The atomic ratio gives empirical formula CH₂O, with formula mass 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. The molecular mass is 180, so the multiplier is 180 ÷ 30 = 6. The molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.
questions.explanation: The atomic ratio gives empirical formula CH₂O, with formula mass 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. The molecular mass is 180, so the multiplier is 180 ÷ 30 = 6. The molecular formula is C₆H₁₂O₆.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
An organic compound X has relative molecular mass 180. It is a colourless crystalline solid, readily soluble in water, containing C, H and O in the atomic ratio 1:2:1. It has a sweet taste and melts on heating. In the presence of yeast and absence of air, X forms compound Y and a colourless gas. Y reacts with sodium to release gas Z, which gives a pop with a lighted splint. Y also reacts with ethanoic acid to form a sweet-smelling compound W.

The reaction of X with yeast forms the basis of which industry?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, which relationship connects pressure P, volume V and absolute temperature T?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV = nRT. Rearranging gives P = nR(T/V). Since nR is constant, P is proportional to T/V, with T measured in kelvin.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of ideal gas, PV = nRT. Rearranging gives P = nR(T/V). Since nR is constant, P is proportional to T/V, with T measured in kelvin.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Solid ammonium chloride is heated to about 350 °C at the closed end of a tube. A porous plug separates it from damp neutral litmus paper near the open end. What happens to the paper initially?
questions.ai_explanation: Heating produces ammonia and hydrogen chloride. Ammonia has the lower molar mass and passes through the porous plug faster. It reaches the damp paper first and produces an alkaline response, turning the paper blue.
questions.explanation: Heating produces ammonia and hydrogen chloride. Ammonia has the lower molar mass and passes through the porous plug faster. It reaches the damp paper first and produces an alkaline response, turning the paper blue.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The colour imparted to a flame by calcium ion is
questions.ai_explanation: Calcium produces a brick-red (orange-red) flame. Sodium gives yellow, potassium lilac, and copper a blue-green flame.
questions.explanation: Calcium produces a brick-red (orange-red) flame. Sodium gives yellow, potassium lilac, and copper a blue-green flame.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A CuSO₄ cell with copper electrodes and an AgNO₃ cell with silver electrodes are connected in series. After current flows for 10 minutes, 0.63 g of copper is deposited. What mass of silver is deposited in the same period? [Cu = 63, Ag = 108; assume complete current efficiency]
questions.ai_explanation: The copper amount is 0.63/63 = 0.010 mol. Cu²⁺ needs two electrons per atom, so 0.020 mol of electrons passes through both cells. Ag⁺ needs one electron per atom, giving 0.020 × 108 = 2.16 g of silver.
questions.explanation: The copper amount is 0.63/63 = 0.010 mol. Cu²⁺ needs two electrons per atom, so 0.020 mol of electrons passes through both cells. Ag⁺ needs one electron per atom, giving 0.020 × 108 = 2.16 g of silver.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In Fe + Cu²⁺ → Fe²⁺ + Cu, iron displaces copper from its ions because

options.A: iron is metallic while copper is ionic
options.B: the atomic weight of copper is greater than that of iron
options.C: copper metal has more electrons than iron metal
options.E: iron is higher in the electrochemical series than copper

questions.ai_explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and more readily loses electrons. Fe is oxidised to Fe²⁺ while Cu²⁺ gains those electrons and becomes copper metal.
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper and more readily loses electrons. Fe is oxidised to Fe²⁺ while Cu²⁺ gains those electrons and becomes copper metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the correct IUPAC name of CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₂CH₃?
questions.ai_explanation: Choose the longest chain containing the double bond: it has four carbon atoms. Number from the double-bond end, giving but-1-ene. The CH₃ branch is on carbon 2, so the name is 2-methylbut-1-ene.
questions.explanation: Choose the longest chain containing the double bond: it has four carbon atoms. Number from the double-bond end, giving but-1-ene. The CH₃ branch is on carbon 2, so the name is 2-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Sodium sulfate decahydrate (Na₂SO₄·10H₂O) loses water of crystallisation on exposure to air. This process is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. It differs from deliquescence, in which a solid absorbs enough moisture to dissolve.
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. It differs from deliquescence, in which a solid absorbs enough moisture to dissolve.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following happens during the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride?
questions.ai_explanation: At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Loss of electrons is oxidation. At the cathode, sodium ions gain electrons to form sodium metal.
questions.explanation: At the anode, chloride ions lose electrons: 2Cl⁻ → Cl₂ + 2e⁻. Loss of electrons is oxidation. At the cathode, sodium ions gain electrons to form sodium metal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Crude petroleum pollution on creeks and waterways can be dispersed by

options.A: heating the affected water to boil off the petroleum
options.B: mechanically stirring to dissolve petroleum in water
options.C: pouring organic solvents into the water
options.E: cooling to freeze out the petroleum

questions.ai_explanation: Detergents contain surfactants that help break oil into small droplets dispersed in water. Dispersion does not destroy the oil; real spill treatment uses selected dispersants and considers environmental conditions.
questions.explanation: Detergents contain surfactants that help break oil into small droplets dispersed in water. Dispersion does not destroy the oil; real spill treatment uses selected dispersants and considers environmental conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Solutions X, Y and Z have pH values 3.0, 5.0 and 9.0 respectively. Which statement is correct?

options.C: Y and Z are more acidic than water
options.D: Y is more acidic than X

questions.ai_explanation: Higher pH corresponds to lower hydrogen-ion concentration. Z has the highest pH, 9.0, and is therefore the least acidic. X, with pH 3.0, is more acidic than Y, with pH 5.0.
questions.explanation: Higher pH corresponds to lower hydrogen-ion concentration. Z has the highest pH, 9.0, and is therefore the least acidic. X, with pH 3.0, is more acidic than Y, with pH 5.0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Stainless steel is an alloy containing
questions.ai_explanation: Stainless steel is an iron alloy containing chromium and usually some carbon. Chromium forms a protective surface oxide that improves corrosion resistance.
questions.explanation: Stainless steel is an iron alloy containing chromium and usually some carbon. Chromium forms a protective surface oxide that improves corrosion resistance.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.50 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ exactly neutralises 20 cm³ of 0.10 mol dm⁻³ NaOH?
questions.ai_explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The NaOH amount is 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Half as many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed: 0.001 mol. Its volume is 0.001/0.50 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. The NaOH amount is 0.1 × 20/1000 = 0.002 mol. Half as many moles of H₂SO₄ are needed: 0.001 mol. Its volume is 0.001/0.50 = 0.002 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A student prepares pure Cu(NO₃)₂ crystals starting with CuO. Which reported step is incorrect?

options.A: Some CuO was reacted with excess dilute H₂SO₄
options.C: After cooling, the crystals were separated by filtration
options.D: The crystals were washed with very cold water
options.E: The crystals were allowed to dry

questions.ai_explanation: Copper(II) nitrate requires nitrate ions. CuO reacts with nitric acid to form Cu(NO₃)₂ and water. Sulfuric acid would instead produce copper(II) sulfate, so step A cannot make the requested salt.
questions.explanation: Copper(II) nitrate requires nitrate ions. CuO reacts with nitric acid to form Cu(NO₃)₂ and water. Sulfuric acid would instead produce copper(II) sulfate, so step A cannot make the requested salt.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 25 °C, 3.06 g of KClO₃ saturates 10 cm³ of water. Express the solubility in mol per dm³ of water. [K = 39, Cl = 35.5, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: The formula mass of KClO₃ is 39 + 35.5 + 3×16 = 122.5. The dissolved amount is 3.06/122.5 ≈ 0.0250 mol in 10 cm³ of water. Per dm³ of water, this is 0.0250×100 = 2.50 mol.
questions.explanation: The formula mass of KClO₃ is 39 + 35.5 + 3×16 = 122.5. The dissolved amount is 3.06/122.5 ≈ 0.0250 mol in 10 cm³ of water. Per dm³ of water, this is 0.0250×100 = 2.50 mol.

questions.question: The cracking process is very important in the petroleum industry because it
questions.ai_explanation: Cracking splits larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes. This increases the supply of shorter hydrocarbons useful in petrol and other engine fuels.
questions.explanation: Cracking splits larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller alkanes and alkenes. This increases the supply of shorter hydrocarbons useful in petrol and other engine fuels.

questions.question: Which solution gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution and a green flame test?

questions.question: The mass of an atom is determined by

options.D: the number of neutrons and protons
options.E: the number of neutrons and electrons

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which addition is an acid–base neutralisation reaction?

options.A: Sodium chloride solution to potassium chloride solution
options.D: Nitric acid to potassium nitrate solution
options.E: Nitric acid to potassium hydroxide solution

questions.ai_explanation: Nitric acid supplies H⁺ ions and potassium hydroxide supplies OH⁻ ions. They combine to form water: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. The overall reaction is HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O, producing potassium nitrate and water.
questions.explanation: Nitric acid supplies H⁺ ions and potassium hydroxide supplies OH⁻ ions. They combine to form water: H⁺ + OH⁻ → H₂O. The overall reaction is HNO₃ + KOH → KNO₃ + H₂O, producing potassium nitrate and water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. Which change greatly increases the rate of this reaction under otherwise identical conditions?

options.B: using a greater volume of acid
options.C: using a smaller volume of acid
options.D: placing the reaction vessel in an ice bath

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂. How much zinc remains undissolved when 2.00 g of zinc reacts with 10 cm³ of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄? [Zn = 65, S = 32, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: The reaction is 1:1 in Zn and H₂SO₄. Acid supplied = 1.0×10/1000 = 0.010 mol, which consumes 0.010×65 = 0.65 g of zinc. The zinc remaining is 2.00 − 0.65 = 1.35 g.
questions.explanation: The reaction is 1:1 in Zn and H₂SO₄. Acid supplied = 1.0×10/1000 = 0.010 mol, which consumes 0.010×65 = 0.65 g of zinc. The zinc remaining is 2.00 − 0.65 = 1.35 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: NH₄NO₂ → N₂ + 2H₂O. What volume of nitrogen is produced from 3.20 g of ammonium nitrite at STP? Use a molar gas volume of 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹. [N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: NH₄NO₂ has formula mass 2×14 + 4×1 + 2×16 = 64. Its amount is 3.20/64 = 0.050 mol. The equation produces one mole of N₂ per mole of NH₄NO₂, so the nitrogen volume is 0.050×22.4 = 1.12 dm³.
questions.explanation: NH₄NO₂ has formula mass 2×14 + 4×1 + 2×16 = 64. Its amount is 3.20/64 = 0.050 mol. The equation produces one mole of N₂ per mole of NH₄NO₂, so the nitrogen volume is 0.050×22.4 = 1.12 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question:
Which of these elements will not react with either water or steam?
1. Carbon
2. Oxygen
3. Copper
4. Bromine
5. Zinc
questions.ai_explanation: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam in this comparison. Hot carbon and zinc react with steam. Bromine reacts reversibly with water to form HBr and HOBr, so copper and bromine cannot be the correct pair.
questions.explanation: Oxygen and copper do not react with water or steam in this comparison. Hot carbon and zinc react with steam. Bromine reacts reversibly with water to form HBr and HOBr, so copper and bromine cannot be the correct pair.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Naphthalene melts at 354 K (81 °C). At this temperature its molecules

options.E: become mobile as intermolecular forces holding the solid are overcome

questions.ai_explanation: On melting, naphthalene molecules gain enough energy to move out of their fixed crystal positions. The molecules remain chemically intact; it is the intermolecular attractions holding the solid structure that are overcome.
questions.explanation: On melting, naphthalene molecules gain enough energy to move out of their fixed crystal positions. The molecules remain chemically intact; it is the intermolecular attractions holding the solid structure that are overcome.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the ratio of the number of molecules in 2 g of hydrogen gas to that in 16 g of oxygen gas? [H = 1, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen is H₂: 2 g represents 2/2 = 1 mol of molecules. Oxygen is O₂: 16 g represents 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Molecule counts are proportional to moles, giving 1:0.5 = 2:1.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen is H₂: 2 g represents 2/2 = 1 mol of molecules. Oxygen is O₂: 16 g represents 16/32 = 0.5 mol. Molecule counts are proportional to moles, giving 1:0.5 = 2:1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In which reaction does hydrogen peroxide act as a reducing agent?
questions.ai_explanation: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. In D, oxygen in H₂O₂ changes from −1 to 0 in O₂, while lead changes from +4 in PbO₂ to +2 in Pb(NO₃)₂. In the other reactions peroxide is reduced to water.
questions.explanation: A reducing agent is itself oxidised. In D, oxygen in H₂O₂ changes from −1 to 0 in O₂, while lead changes from +4 in PbO₂ to +2 in Pb(NO₃)₂. In the other reactions peroxide is reduced to water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For the reaction 2Fe³⁺ + 2I⁻ → 2Fe²⁺ + I₂, which statement describes what happens?

options.E: I⁻ removes an electron from Fe³⁺

questions.ai_explanation: Iodide loses electrons: 2I⁻ → I₂ + 2e⁻. Its oxidation number rises from −1 to 0, so it is oxidised. Each Fe³⁺ ion gains an electron to become Fe²⁺, which is reduction.
questions.explanation: Iodide loses electrons: 2I⁻ → I₂ + 2e⁻. Its oxidation number rises from −1 to 0, so it is oxidised. Each Fe³⁺ ion gains an electron to become Fe²⁺, which is reduction.

questions.question: The energy profile represents A + B → C + D. Which description of the forward reaction follows from it?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In dilute solution, NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O has an enthalpy change of −57.3 kJ for the equation as written. Using the same dilute strong-acid/strong-base neutralisation approximation, what is the enthalpy change for 2NaOH + H₂SO₄ → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O?
questions.ai_explanation: The reference reaction forms one mole of water and releases 57.3 kJ. The second equation forms two moles of water. In the stated dilute neutralisation approximation, ΔH = 2 × (−57.3) = −114.6 kJ. The negative sign indicates heat released.
questions.explanation: The reference reaction forms one mole of water and releases 57.3 kJ. The second equation forms two moles of water. In the stated dilute neutralisation approximation, ΔH = 2 × (−57.3) = −114.6 kJ. The negative sign indicates heat released.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Limewater, used to detect carbon dioxide in the laboratory, is an aqueous solution of
questions.ai_explanation: Limewater is a clear aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. Carbon dioxide produces suspended calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, making it milky.
questions.explanation: Limewater is a clear aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂. Carbon dioxide produces suspended calcium carbonate: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃ + H₂O, making it milky.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is not true of carbon monoxide under ordinary uncatalysed conditions?

options.B: CO is readily oxidised by air at room temperature to form CO₂
options.C: CO can be prepared by passing CO₂ over coke heated to about 1000 °C
options.D: CO can be prepared by heating charcoal with a limited supply of oxygen
options.E: CO is a good reducing agent

questions.ai_explanation: CO does not readily combine with air at room temperature without suitable activation or catalysis. It can burn to CO₂ when ignited. It is poisonous and can act as a reducing agent, so B is the false statement.
questions.explanation: CO does not readily combine with air at room temperature without suitable activation or catalysis. It can burn to CO₂ when ignited. It is poisonous and can act as a reducing agent, so B is the false statement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: From ZnO + Na₂O → Na₂ZnO₂ and ZnO + CO₂ → ZnCO₃, zinc oxide may be classified as
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc oxide reacts with a basic oxide, Na₂O, and with an acidic oxide, CO₂. An oxide that can show both acidic and basic behaviour is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An example of a neutral oxide is
questions.ai_explanation: Carbon monoxide is classified as a neutral oxide in ordinary acid-base chemistry. CO₂, SO₂ and NO₂ are acidic oxides, while Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is classified as a neutral oxide in ordinary acid-base chemistry. CO₂, SO₂ and NO₂ are acidic oxides, while Al₂O₃ is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In 3Cl₂ + 2NH₃ → N₂ + 6HCl, ammonia acts as

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In the Haber process for manufacturing ammonia, finely divided iron is used as
questions.ai_explanation: Iron provides a catalytic surface that speeds up the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to make ammonia. It changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not the equilibrium composition.
questions.explanation: Iron provides a catalytic surface that speeds up the reaction of nitrogen with hydrogen to make ammonia. It changes the rate of reaching equilibrium, not the equilibrium composition.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A compound has vapour density 56.5 relative to hydrogen and composition C 53.1%, N 12.4%, O 28.3%, H 6.2%. What is its molecular formula? [C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, H = 1]

Dividing by the smallest gives C:H:O:N ≈ 5:7:2:1. C₅H₇O₂N has formula mass 113, so it is also the molecular formula.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When a kerosene fraction from petroleum is heated strongly and converted into a lower-boiling liquid, the process is known as
questions.ai_explanation: Cracking uses heat, often with a catalyst, to break larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones. The smaller products generally have lower boiling points.
questions.explanation: Cracking uses heat, often with a catalyst, to break larger hydrocarbon molecules into smaller ones. The smaller products generally have lower boiling points.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The compound CH₃CH₂C(=O)OH is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Alkaline hydrolysis of naturally occurring fats and oils yields.

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.question: Alkaline hydrolysis of fats and oils produces soap and
questions.ai_explanation: Fats and oils are esters of glycerol. Alkaline hydrolysis breaks their ester links to give fatty-acid salts, which are soaps, and glycerol. Glycerol has an OH group on each of its three carbons, so its name is propane-1,2,3-triol.

questions.question: Which listed gas is a major cause of gas explosions in coal mines?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A 10.0 dm³ air sample at STP contains H₂S. Passing it through excess Pb(NO₃)₂ solution gives 5.02 g of PbS. Using Pb(NO₃)₂ + H₂S → PbS + 2HNO₃, calculate the percentage by volume of H₂S. [Pb = 207, S = 32; molar gas volume at STP = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: Pb(NO₃)₂ + H₂S → PbS + 2HNO₃ gives one mole of PbS per mole of H₂S. The PbS molar mass is 207 + 32 = 239 g mol⁻¹, so the H₂S amount is 5.02/239 mol. Its STP volume is about 0.470 dm³, giving (0.470/10.0)×100 = 4.70% by volume.
questions.explanation: Pb(NO₃)₂ + H₂S → PbS + 2HNO₃ gives one mole of PbS per mole of H₂S. The PbS molar mass is 207 + 32 = 239 g mol⁻¹, so the H₂S amount is 5.02/239 mol. Its STP volume is about 0.470 dm³, giving (0.470/10.0)×100 = 4.70% by volume.

questions.question: Which listed contaminant is particularly associated with effluent from a brine-electrolysis plant using a flowing mercury cathode?

options.C: Gas or liquid particles dispersed in liquid

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A 2.0 g sample of a monobasic acid is made up to 250 cm³ with water. A 25.00 cm³ portion requires 20.00 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH for complete neutralisation. What is the acid’s molar mass?
questions.ai_explanation: The 25.00 cm³ aliquot contains 0.02000×0.1 = 0.00200 mol of acid because the acid is monobasic. The full 250 cm³ contains ten times as much, or 0.0200 mol. Its molar mass is 2.0/0.0200 = 100 g mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the hydrogen-ion concentration of a dilute solution with pH 4.398?
questions.ai_explanation: For the usual dilute-solution calculation, [H⁺] = 10⁻ᵖᴴ. With pH 4.398, [H⁺] = 10⁻⁴·³⁹⁸ ≈ 4.0×10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³. A change of one pH unit corresponds to a tenfold concentration change.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A charge of 0.1 faraday deposits 2.95 g of nickel from an aqueous solution. How many moles will 0.4 faraday deposit under the same conditions? [Ni = 58.7]
questions.ai_explanation: Deposited nickel is proportional to charge. Increasing from 0.1 to 0.4 faraday deposits four times the mass: 4×2.95 = 11.8 g. The amount is 11.8/58.7 ≈ 0.20 mol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 6Fe²⁺ + 14H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 6Fe³⁺ + 7H₂O, how does chromium’s oxidation number change?
questions.ai_explanation: For Cr₂O₇²⁻, let chromium’s oxidation number be x: 2x + 7(−2) = −2, so x = +6. The product is Cr³⁺, whose oxidation number is +3. Chromium is therefore reduced from +6 to +3.
questions.explanation: For Cr₂O₇²⁻, let chromium’s oxidation number be x: 2x + 7(−2) = −2, so x = +6. The product is Cr³⁺, whose oxidation number is +3. Chromium is therefore reduced from +6 to +3.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Fe₂O₃(s) + 2Al(s) → Al₂O₃(s) + 2Fe(s). The enthalpies of formation of Al₂O₃(s) and Fe₂O₃(s) are −1670 and −822 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively. What is the enthalpy change for the reaction as written?
questions.ai_explanation: Use formation enthalpies of products minus those of reactants. Aluminium and iron in their elemental reference states contribute zero. Thus ΔH = [−1670 + 2(0)] − [−822 + 2(0)] = −848 kJ. There is one mole of Al₂O₃ in the balanced equation.
questions.explanation: Use formation enthalpies of products minus those of reactants. Aluminium and iron in their elemental reference states contribute zero. Thus ΔH = [−1670 + 2(0)] − [−822 + 2(0)] = −848 kJ. There is one mole of Al₂O₃ in the balanced equation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Iron galvanised with zinc receives cathodic protection because

options.A: Zinc has a more positive oxidation potential than iron
options.B: Zinc has a less positive oxidation potential than iron
options.C: Both have the same oxidation potential

questions.question: Why is a coal fire dangerous in a poorly ventilated room?

questions.question: An iron ore contains 70.0% Fe₂O₃ by mass. What mass of iron can theoretically be obtained from 80 kg of this ore? [Fe = 56, O = 16]

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In two experiments, 0.36 g and 0.71 g of chlorine combine with 0.20 g and 0.40 g of a metal X, respectively. Which law is supported by these mass data, allowing for their reported precision?
questions.ai_explanation: The chlorine-to-metal mass ratios are 0.36/0.20 = 1.80 and 0.71/0.40 = 1.775. These are approximately the same at the precision of the reported masses. The data therefore support constant composition: the elements combine in essentially the same mass proportion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of CO₂ at STP is produced by complete thermal decomposition of 1 kg of KHCO₃? [K = 39, H = 1, C = 12, O = 16; molar gas volume at STP = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: The balanced decomposition is 2KHCO₃ → K₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. KHCO₃ has molar mass 100 g mol⁻¹, so 1 kg is 10 mol. Every two moles give one mole of CO₂; 5 mol therefore occupy 5×22.4 = 112 dm³ at STP.
questions.explanation: The balanced decomposition is 2KHCO₃ → K₂CO₃ + H₂O + CO₂. KHCO₃ has molar mass 100 g mol⁻¹, so 1 kg is 10 mol. Every two moles give one mole of CO₂; 5 mol therefore occupy 5×22.4 = 112 dm³ at STP.

questions.question: Atoms of X have two outer-shell electrons and atoms of Y have seven. For their expected ionic compound, which statement is false?

options.B: It is likely to be ionic

questions.question: X⁻ and Y⁺ each contain 10 electrons. How many protons are in the nuclei of X and Y, respectively?

options.B: H3O+ acts as an oxidizing agent

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the molar concentration of a solution containing 4.0 g of sodium hydroxide in 250 cm³ of solution?
questions.ai_explanation: The molar mass of NaOH is 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻¹. Thus 4.0 g is 0.10 mol. The solution volume is 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³, giving 0.10/0.250 = 0.40 mol dm⁻³.
questions.explanation: The molar mass of NaOH is 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻¹. Thus 4.0 g is 0.10 mol. The solution volume is 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³, giving 0.10/0.250 = 0.40 mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Standard reduction potentials are: Cu²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Cu(s), +0.34 V; Fe²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Fe(s), −0.44 V; Ba²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Ba(s), −2.90 V; Zn²⁺(aq) + 2e⁻ → Zn(s), −0.76 V. Which metal is the most powerful reducing agent?
questions.ai_explanation: The more negative the standard reduction potential, the greater the tendency of the metal to be oxidised in the reverse process. Barium has the most negative value, −2.90 V, so it is the strongest reducing agent in this comparison.
questions.explanation: The more negative the standard reduction potential, the greater the tendency of the metal to be oxidised in the reverse process. Barium has the most negative value, −2.90 V, so it is the strongest reducing agent in this comparison.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The oxidation states of chlorine in HOCl, HClO₃ and HClO₄ are respectively
questions.ai_explanation: Take hydrogen as +1 and oxygen as −2. Each neutral molecule has total oxidation number zero: chlorine is +1 in HOCl, +5 in HClO₃ and +7 in HClO₄.
questions.explanation: Take hydrogen as +1 and oxygen as −2. Each neutral molecule has total oxidation number zero: chlorine is +1 in HOCl, +5 in HClO₃ and +7 in HClO₄.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The standard enthalpies of formation of CO₂(g), H₂O(g) and CO(g) are −394, −242 and −110 kJ mol⁻¹ respectively. What is the standard enthalpy change for CO(g) + H₂O(g) → CO₂(g) + H₂(g)?
questions.ai_explanation: Use ΔH° = sum of product formation enthalpies minus sum of reactant formation enthalpies. H₂(g) has zero standard formation enthalpy, so ΔH° = (−394 + 0) − (−110 − 242) = −42 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Use ΔH° = sum of product formation enthalpies minus sum of reactant formation enthalpies. H₂(g) has zero standard formation enthalpy, so ΔH° = (−394 + 0) − (−110 − 242) = −42 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 10 g of a solid is in equilibrium with its own vapour. At the same temperature, another 1 g of the solid is added. Its equilibrium vapour pressure will
questions.ai_explanation: At a fixed temperature, the equilibrium vapour pressure of a pure solid is independent of how much solid is present, provided some solid remains. Adding 1 g therefore leaves the equilibrium vapour pressure unchanged.
questions.explanation: At a fixed temperature, the equilibrium vapour pressure of a pure solid is independent of how much solid is present, provided some solid remains. Adding 1 g therefore leaves the equilibrium vapour pressure unchanged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Two energy profiles, X and Y, describe the same homogeneous gaseous reaction. Energy is plotted against reaction progress. Both profiles start at the same reactant energy and end at the same, lower product energy. Y has a lower peak than X. Which change produces profile Y?

options.B: Increase in the concentration of a reactant

questions.ai_explanation: A catalyst provides a reaction pathway with a lower activation-energy barrier. It does not change the energies of the reactants and products, so the reaction enthalpy remains the same.
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a reaction pathway with a lower activation-energy barrier. It does not change the energies of the reactants and products, so the reaction enthalpy remains the same.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: NaCl(s) + H₂SO₄(l) → HCl(g) + NaHSO₄(s). In this reaction, H₂SO₄ behaves as

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which salt produces its metal, oxygen and nitrogen(IV) oxide on heating?
questions.ai_explanation: Silver nitrate decomposes to silver, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen: 2AgNO₃ → 2Ag + 2NO₂ + O₂. Sodium nitrate gives a nitrite and oxygen, while the calcium and lithium salts give their metal oxides rather than the metals.
questions.explanation: Silver nitrate decomposes to silver, nitrogen dioxide and oxygen: 2AgNO₃ → 2Ag + 2NO₂ + O₂. Sodium nitrate gives a nitrite and oxygen, while the calcium and lithium salts give their metal oxides rather than the metals.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An experiment produces a mixture of CO₂ and CO. Which treatment removes CO₂ while retaining CO?

options.A: Pass it over heated copper(II) oxide
options.B: Bubble it through concentrated sulfuric acid
options.C: Bubble it through sodium hydroxide solution

questions.ai_explanation: Sodium hydroxide absorbs the acidic oxide CO₂, while CO does not react in this washing step. With sufficient hydroxide, CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Passing the mixture over hot CuO would instead consume CO by oxidising it to CO₂.
questions.explanation: Sodium hydroxide absorbs the acidic oxide CO₂, while CO does not react in this washing step. With sufficient hydroxide, CO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂CO₃ + H₂O. Passing the mixture over hot CuO would instead consume CO by oxidising it to CO₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which property identifies chloride ions from an ionic chloride in aqueous solution?

options.A: They can be decomposed by heat
options.B: They react with aqueous AgNO₃ to give a white precipitate soluble in excess ammonia
options.C: They explode on contact with dry ammonia gas
options.D: They react with concentrated sulfuric acid to give white fumes of chlorine gas

questions.ai_explanation: Chloride ions give a white silver chloride precipitate with aqueous silver nitrate: Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s). Excess ammonia dissolves it by forming the soluble complex [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺.
questions.explanation: Chloride ions give a white silver chloride precipitate with aqueous silver nitrate: Ag⁺ + Cl⁻ → AgCl(s). Excess ammonia dissolves it by forming the soluble complex [Ag(NH₃)₂]⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Dilute aqueous solutions of lead(II) nitrate and potassium bromide are mixed and a precipitate forms. Which list gives the resulting solid and dissolved spectator species?
questions.ai_explanation: Lead(II) ions and bromide ions form insoluble lead(II) bromide: Pb²⁺ + 2Br⁻ → PbBr₂(s). Potassium and nitrate ions remain in solution as spectator ions. The full reaction is Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KBr → PbBr₂ + 2KNO₃.
questions.explanation: Lead(II) ions and bromide ions form insoluble lead(II) bromide: Pb²⁺ + 2Br⁻ → PbBr₂(s). Potassium and nitrate ions remain in solution as spectator ions. The full reaction is Pb(NO₃)₂ + 2KBr → PbBr₂ + 2KNO₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Bronze is an alloy of

questions.explanation: Traditional bronze is an alloy of copper and tin. Copper and zinc form brass, which is a different alloy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Copper reacts with concentrated nitric acid to give which set of products?
questions.ai_explanation: Concentrated nitric acid oxidises copper to copper(II) nitrate and is reduced mainly to nitrogen dioxide. The balanced equation is Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O.
questions.explanation: Concentrated nitric acid oxidises copper to copper(II) nitrate and is reduced mainly to nitrogen dioxide. The balanced equation is Cu + 4HNO₃ → Cu(NO₃)₂ + 2NO₂ + 2H₂O.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Al₂O₃(s) + 3H₂SO₄(aq) → Al₂(SO₄)₃(aq) + 3H₂O(l). Al₂O₃(s) + 2NaOH(aq) + 3H₂O(l) → 2NaAl(OH)₄(aq). These reactions show that Al₂O₃ is

questions.explanation: Aluminium oxide reacts with sulfuric acid and also with sodium hydroxide. An oxide that reacts with both acids and bases is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The fraction of crude oil used as jet fuel is

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.question: Why is tetraethyllead undesirable as an antiknock additive?

options.B: It causes pollution through exhaust emissions
options.C: It lowers the octane rating of petrol

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Palm wine turns sour with time because

options.A: Its sugar content is converted into alcohol
options.B: The carbon dioxide formed during fermentation has a sour taste
options.C: It is commonly adulterated by tappers and sellers
options.D: Microbial activity produces organic acids in it

questions.explanation: Microorganisms produce organic acids during continued palm-wine fermentation. For example, acetic-acid bacteria can oxidise ethanol to ethanoic acid, increasing acidity and producing a sour taste.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 8 g of CH₄ occupies 11.2 dm³ at s.t.p. What volume would 22 g of CH₃CH₂CH₃ occupy under the same conditions? [C = 12, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: CH₄ has molar mass 16 g mol⁻¹, so 8 g contains 0.5 mol. CH₃CH₂CH₃ has molar mass 44 g mol⁻¹, so 22 g also contains 0.5 mol. Equal amounts of gas occupy equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure: 11.2 dm³.
questions.explanation: CH₄ has molar mass 16 g mol⁻¹, so 8 g contains 0.5 mol. CH₃CH₂CH₃ has molar mass 44 g mol⁻¹, so 22 g also contains 0.5 mol. Equal amounts of gas occupy equal volumes at the same temperature and pressure: 11.2 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: To what temperature must a fixed amount of gas initially at 273 K be heated to double both its volume and pressure?
questions.ai_explanation: For a fixed amount of gas, PV/T is constant. Doubling both pressure and volume multiplies PV by four, so the absolute temperature must become 4 × 273 = 1092 K.
questions.explanation: For a fixed amount of gas, PV/T is constant. Doubling both pressure and volume multiplies PV by four, so the absolute temperature must become 4 × 273 = 1092 K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A gas has relative molecular mass 2Y. Using the hydrogen-reference convention for vapour density, what is Y?

options.B: The vapour density of the gas

questions.ai_explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen compares the masses of equal gas volumes at the same temperature and pressure. Since hydrogen has relative molecular mass 2, Mr = 2 × vapour density. Thus Y is the vapour density.
questions.explanation: Vapour density relative to hydrogen compares the masses of equal gas volumes at the same temperature and pressure. Since hydrogen has relative molecular mass 2, Mr = 2 × vapour density. Thus Y is the vapour density.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At the same temperature and pressure, gases X and Y have densities 0.5 g dm⁻³ and 2.0 g dm⁻³ respectively. What is the rate of diffusion of X relative to Y?
questions.ai_explanation: By Graham’s law, diffusion rate is inversely proportional to the square root of gas density under the same conditions. Hence rate(X)/rate(Y) = √(2.0/0.5) = √4 = 2.0.
questions.explanation: By Graham’s law, diffusion rate is inversely proportional to the square root of gas density under the same conditions. Hence rate(X)/rate(Y) = √(2.0/0.5) = √4 = 2.0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Heating a gas in a fixed-volume container increases its pressure because

options.B: The gas molecules bombard the container walls more frequently
options.C: It increases the number of collisions between molecules
options.D: It causes the molecules to combine

questions.ai_explanation: Heating increases the average kinetic energy of the gas molecules. In a fixed-volume container they strike its walls more frequently and with greater momentum, increasing the pressure.
questions.explanation: Heating increases the average kinetic energy of the gas molecules. In a fixed-volume container they strike its walls more frequently and with greater momentum, increasing the pressure.

questions.question: Which of these properties generally decreases down a group in the periodic table?

questions.explanation: Deuterium is hydrogen-2. A neutral deuterium atom has one proton, one neutron and one electron, giving mass number 2 and atomic number 1.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds is a base?
questions.ai_explanation: Calcium oxide is a basic oxide: it neutralises acids to form a salt and water, for example CaO + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + H₂O. CO₂ is an acidic oxide, while H₃PO₃ and CH₃COOH are acids.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of oxygen at s.t.p. is liberated by 9650 C during electrolysis, assuming the charge is used for oxygen evolution? [Molar gas volume = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹; F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: Producing one mole of O₂ from water or hydroxide requires four moles of electrons. The charge supplies 9650/96500 = 0.100 mol electrons, giving 0.0250 mol O₂. At s.t.p., its volume is 0.0250 × 22.4 = 0.560 dm³.
questions.explanation: Producing one mole of O₂ from water or hydroxide requires four moles of electrons. The charge supplies 9650/96500 = 0.100 mol electrons, giving 0.0250 mol O₂. At s.t.p., its volume is 0.0250 × 22.4 = 0.560 dm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In electrolytic purification using a copper(II) chloride solution, crude copper should be

options.A: Both the anode and the cathode

questions.ai_explanation: The impure copper is the anode, where copper dissolves by oxidation: Cu → Cu²⁺ + 2e⁻. Copper ions are reduced and deposited on a separate cathode. This transfers copper away from the impure electrode.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: H⁻ + H₂O(l) → H₂(g) + OH⁻(aq). What can be inferred?

options.A: The reaction is a double decomposition
options.B: The hydride ion is a reducing agent
options.C: The hydride ion is an oxidising agent

questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen in H⁻ has oxidation number −1 and becomes 0 in H₂. The hydride ion is oxidised, so it acts as the reducing agent. Hydrogen from water is reduced from +1 to 0.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen in H⁻ has oxidation number −1 and becomes 0 in H₂. The hydride ion is oxidised, so it acts as the reducing agent. Hydrogen from water is reduced from +1 to 0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: MnO₄⁻(aq) + 8H⁺(aq) + 5Fe²⁺(aq) → Mn²⁺(aq) + 5Fe³⁺(aq) + 4H₂O(l). How does the oxidation number of manganese change?

questions.explanation: In MnO₄⁻, four oxygen atoms contribute −8. The ion has charge −1, so manganese is +7. In Mn²⁺ it is +2, giving a change from +7 to +2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is true for an exothermic reaction at equilibrium?

options.A: Increasing temperature increases the equilibrium constant
options.B: Increasing temperature decreases the equilibrium constant
options.C: Adding a catalyst increases the equilibrium constant
options.D: Adding a catalyst decreases the equilibrium constant

questions.ai_explanation: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing temperature favours the reverse, endothermic direction. The equilibrium constant for the forward reaction decreases. A catalyst changes the rate of reaching equilibrium but not the equilibrium constant.
questions.explanation: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing temperature favours the reverse, endothermic direction. The equilibrium constant for the forward reaction decreases. A catalyst changes the rate of reaching equilibrium but not the equilibrium constant.

questions.question: Which solution gives a white precipitate with barium chloride solution acidified with hydrochloric acid?
questions.ai_explanation: Sulfate ions form white barium sulfate, which remains insoluble in dilute hydrochloric acid: Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄(s). Acid removes interference from carbonate and sulfite by converting them into gaseous products.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Why is SO₃ not dissolved directly in water during manufacture of H₂SO₄ by the Contact process?

options.A: The reaction of SO₃ with water is violently exothermic
options.B: Acid is usually added to water, never water to acid
options.C: SO₃ does not dissolve readily in water

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In an electrolytic arrangement used to protect iron from corrosion, the iron is

options.C: Used with a metal of lower electropositive potential

questions.question: When sodium is added to ethanol, the products are

questions.question: When sodium ethanoate is treated with a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid, one product is

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which reaction represents saponification?

options.A: Carboxylic acids reacting with sodium hydroxide
options.D: Alkanoate esters reacting with sodium hydroxide

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: How many H⁺ ions can 4.9 g of H₂SO₄ provide if both acidic hydrogens are completely released? [S = 32, O = 16, H = 1; Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹]

questions.question: What volume of oxygen remains after complete reaction of 8 cm³ of hydrogen with 20 cm³ of oxygen, with all gas volumes compared at the same temperature and pressure?

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.ai_explanation: The equation shows one mole, or one gas volume at equal conditions, of propane requires five of oxygen. Therefore 50 cm³ propane needs 5 × 50 = 250 cm³ oxygen.
questions.explanation: The equation shows one mole, or one gas volume at equal conditions, of propane requires five of oxygen. Therefore 50 cm³ propane needs 5 × 50 = 250 cm³ oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 30 cm³ of hydrogen is collected over water at 27 °C and total pressure 780 mmHg. Taking the given water-vapour pressure as 10 mmHg, calculate the dry hydrogen volume at 760 mmHg and 7 °C. Use T(K) = t(°C) + 273.
questions.ai_explanation: The initial hydrogen partial pressure is 780 − 10 = 770 mmHg. Use absolute temperatures 300 K and 280 K: V₂ = 30 × (770/760) × (280/300) = 28.37 cm³, or 28.4 cm³.
questions.explanation: The initial hydrogen partial pressure is 780 − 10 = 770 mmHg. Use absolute temperatures 300 K and 280 K: V₂ = 30 × (770/760) × (280/300) = 28.37 cm³, or 28.4 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Sulfur dioxide and methane are released simultaneously at opposite ends of a narrow tube under the same conditions. What is the ratio R(SO₂):R(CH₄)? [S = 32, O = 16, C = 12, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: M(SO₂) = 32 + 2(16) = 64 g mol⁻¹ and M(CH₄) = 12 + 4 = 16 g mol⁻¹. Graham’s law gives R(SO₂)/R(CH₄) = √(16/64) = 1/2. Thus the rate ratio is 1:2.
questions.explanation: M(SO₂) = 32 + 2(16) = 64 g mol⁻¹ and M(CH₄) = 12 + 4 = 16 g mol⁻¹. Graham’s law gives R(SO₂)/R(CH₄) = √(16/64) = 1/2. Thus the rate ratio is 1:2.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An atom is shown with four occupied electron shells and two electrons in the outermost shell. When it combines with chlorine, which type of bond is formed?
questions.ai_explanation: The two outer electrons can be transferred to two chlorine atoms. This produces a metal cation and chloride anions, held together by electrostatic attraction: an ionic, or electrovalent, bond.
questions.explanation: The two outer electrons can be transferred to two chlorine atoms. This produces a metal cation and chloride anions, held together by electrostatic attraction: an ionic, or electrovalent, bond.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The lines in the hydrogen emission spectrum result from emission of
questions.ai_explanation: An electron moving from a higher to a lower energy level emits a photon with energy equal to the level difference. Hydrogen’s discrete energy levels produce separate spectral lines.
questions.explanation: An electron moving from a higher to a lower energy level emits a photon with energy equal to the level difference. Hydrogen’s discrete energy levels produce separate spectral lines.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which property is used to separate nitrogen and oxygen by industrial fractional distillation of liquid air?
questions.ai_explanation: Fractional distillation of liquid air separates nitrogen and oxygen because they have different boiling points. The more volatile nitrogen boils off before oxygen.
questions.explanation: Fractional distillation of liquid air separates nitrogen and oxygen because they have different boiling points. The more volatile nitrogen boils off before oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Excess phosphorus is burned in a gas jar of air. The residual gas passes through concentrated KOH solution and then concentrated H₂SO₄. Which gases are collected?

options.A: Carbon dioxide, nitrogen and noble gases
options.D: Carbon dioxide, nitrogen dioxide and noble gases

questions.ai_explanation: Burning excess phosphorus removes oxygen from the air. Potassium hydroxide absorbs carbon dioxide and other acidic oxides, and concentrated sulfuric acid removes water vapour. Nitrogen and the noble gases remain.
questions.explanation: Burning excess phosphorus removes oxygen from the air. Potassium hydroxide absorbs carbon dioxide and other acidic oxides, and concentrated sulfuric acid removes water vapour. Nitrogen and the noble gases remain.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Soap lather is a colloid in which
questions.ai_explanation: Soap lather is a foam: bubbles of gas are dispersed through a liquid film. Thus its dispersed phase is gas and its continuous phase is liquid.
questions.explanation: Soap lather is a foam: bubbles of gas are dispersed through a liquid film. Thus its dispersed phase is gas and its continuous phase is liquid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 25 °C, what is the pH after mixing 100 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ HCl with 100 cm³ of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ NaOH, assuming additive volumes?
questions.ai_explanation: Initial amounts are 0.010 mol HCl and 0.020 mol NaOH. After neutralisation, 0.010 mol OH⁻ remains in 0.200 dm³, so [OH⁻] = 0.050 mol dm⁻³. pOH = 1.30 and pH = 14.00 − 1.30 = 12.70.
questions.explanation: Initial amounts are 0.010 mol HCl and 0.020 mol NaOH. After neutralisation, 0.010 mol OH⁻ remains in 0.200 dm³, so [OH⁻] = 0.050 mol dm⁻³. pOH = 1.30 and pH = 14.00 − 1.30 = 12.70.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ sulfuric acid is needed to react completely with 2.86 g of sodium carbonate decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O? [Na = 23, C = 12, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: M(Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) = 106 + 180 = 286 g mol⁻¹. The sample contains 2.86/286 = 0.0100 mol carbonate. H₂SO₄ reacts with carbonate in a 1:1 ratio, so the required volume is 0.0100/0.100 = 0.100 dm³ = 100 cm³.
questions.explanation: M(Na₂CO₃·10H₂O) = 106 + 180 = 286 g mol⁻¹. The sample contains 2.86/286 = 0.0100 mol carbonate. H₂SO₄ reacts with carbonate in a 1:1 ratio, so the required volume is 0.0100/0.100 = 0.100 dm³ = 100 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What mass of gold is deposited from gold(III) sulfate when 15 A passes for 193 s, assuming full current efficiency? [Au = 197; F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: The charge is Q = It = 15 × 193 = 2895 C, equivalent to 0.0300 mol electrons. Gold(III) needs three electrons per atom, so 0.0100 mol gold is deposited. Its mass is 0.0100 × 197 = 1.97 g.
questions.explanation: The charge is Q = It = 15 × 193 = 2895 C, equivalent to 0.0300 mol electrons. Gold(III) needs three electrons per atom, so 0.0100 mol gold is deposited. Its mass is 0.0100 × 197 = 1.97 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Fe(s) + Cu²⁺(aq) → Fe²⁺(aq) + Cu(s). Which statement follows?
questions.ai_explanation: Cu²⁺ gains two electrons to form copper, so it is reduced. The substance that accepts electrons and causes the other substance to be oxidised is the oxidising agent.
questions.explanation: Cu²⁺ gains two electrons to form copper, so it is reduced. The substance that accepts electrons and causes the other substance to be oxidised is the oxidising agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In 2FeCl₂(s) + Cl₂(g) → 2FeCl₃(s), which is the reducing agent?
questions.ai_explanation: Iron changes from +2 in FeCl₂ to +3 in FeCl₃. FeCl₂ is therefore oxidised and supplies the electrons that reduce chlorine, making it the reducing agent.
questions.explanation: Iron changes from +2 in FeCl₂ to +3 in FeCl₃. FeCl₂ is therefore oxidised and supplies the electrons that reduce chlorine, making it the reducing agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An energy diagram for P₂ + Q₂ → 2PQ places reactants at 10 kJ, products at 15 kJ and the peak at 40 kJ. What is the activation energy for the backward reaction?
questions.ai_explanation: For the backward reaction, the starting energy is the product level, 15 kJ. The peak is 40 kJ, so the backward activation energy is 40 − 15 = 25 kJ.
questions.explanation: For the backward reaction, the starting energy is the product level, 15 kJ. The peak is 40 kJ, so the backward activation energy is 40 − 15 = 25 kJ.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For 2X(g) + Y(g) → Z(g), the rate of formation of Z is independent of [Y] and quadruples when [X] doubles. Which rate law agrees?
questions.ai_explanation: Independence from [Y] means order zero in Y. Doubling [X] multiplies the rate by four, so 2ⁿ = 4 and n = 2. Therefore R = k[X]²[Y]⁰ = k[X]².
questions.explanation: Independence from [Y] means order zero in Y. Doubling [X] multiplies the rate by four, so 2ⁿ = 4 and n = 2. Therefore R = k[X]²[Y]⁰ = k[X]².

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 2Cl₂(g) + 2H₂O(g) ⇌ 4HCl(g) + O₂(g), ΔH° = +115 kJ mol⁻¹. How does decreasing temperature affect the equilibrium?

options.D: Doubles the rate of the reverse reaction

questions.explanation: The positive ΔH means the forward reaction absorbs heat. Cooling favours the exothermic reverse direction, shifting the equilibrium towards chlorine and water vapour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Consider: (i) 3CuO(s) + 2NH₃(g) → 3Cu(s) + 3H₂O(l) + N₂(g); (ii) 2NH₃(g) + 3Cl₂(g) → 6HCl(g) + N₂(g); (iii) 4NH₃(g) + 3O₂(g) → 6H₂O(l) + 2N₂(g). Which property of ammonia do these reactions demonstrate?
questions.ai_explanation: Nitrogen in NH₃ has oxidation number −3 and becomes 0 in N₂ in each equation. Ammonia is oxidised while the other reactant is reduced, demonstrating that ammonia acts as a reducing agent.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen in NH₃ has oxidation number −3 and becomes 0 in N₂ in each equation. Ammonia is oxidised while the other reactant is reduced, demonstrating that ammonia acts as a reducing agent.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A heated flask contains solution X. A delivery tube carries the gas from the flask into an inverted water-filled receiver, where nitrogen gas (N₂) is collected over water. Which mixture could X contain?
questions.ai_explanation: On warming, sodium nitrite and ammonium chloride produce nitrogen: NaNO₂ + NH₄Cl → NaCl + N₂ + 2H₂O. The ammonium and nitrite ions together supply the two nitrogen atoms. Nitrogen is only slightly soluble in water, allowing collection by displacement of water. Nitrate and nitrite are different ions, NO₃⁻ and NO₂⁻ respectively.

Nitrogen is only slightly soluble in water, allowing collection by displacement of water. Nitrate and nitrite are different ions, NO₃⁻ and NO₂⁻ respectively.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is observed when aqueous iron(III) chloride is mixed with aqueous sodium hydroxide?
questions.ai_explanation: Iron(III) ions form insoluble, reddish-brown iron(III) hydroxide: Fe³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Fe(OH)₃(s). Iron remains in oxidation state +3; this is precipitation, not reduction to iron(II). Sodium and chloride ions remain in solution.
questions.explanation: Iron(III) ions form insoluble, reddish-brown iron(III) hydroxide: Fe³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Fe(OH)₃(s). Iron remains in oxidation state +3; this is precipitation, not reduction to iron(II). Sodium and chloride ions remain in solution.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Why are alloys often preferred to pure metals for practical applications?

options.C: Useful metallic properties can be improved by alloying
options.D: All alloys are mixtures only of metals

questions.ai_explanation: Alloying can improve properties needed for a use, such as hardness, strength or corrosion resistance. This is why a suitable alloy may be chosen over a pure metal; the improvement depends on the alloy and application.
questions.explanation: Alloying can improve properties needed for a use, such as hardness, strength or corrosion resistance. This is why a suitable alloy may be chosen over a pure metal; the improvement depends on the alloy and application.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH(CH₃)₂?
questions.ai_explanation: The longest chain containing the OH group has five carbons. The OH group is at carbon 3 whichever end is used, so choose the direction that gives the methyl substituent position 2 rather than 4. The name is 2-methylpentan-3-ol.
questions.explanation: The longest chain containing the OH group has five carbons. The OH group is at carbon 3 whichever end is used, so choose the direction that gives the methyl substituent position 2 rather than 4. The name is 2-methylpentan-3-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ethene undergoes addition polymerisation with oxygen used as an initiator: nCH₂=CH₂ → [–CH₂–CH₂–]ₙ. Which material is produced?
questions.ai_explanation: Ethene monomers join by addition polymerisation. Their double bonds open to form the repeating unit –CH₂–CH₂–, giving polyethene, commonly called polythene.
questions.explanation: Ethene monomers join by addition polymerisation. Their double bonds open to form the repeating unit –CH₂–CH₂–, giving polyethene, commonly called polythene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What are the products of complete combustion of a pure hydrocarbon in excess oxygen?
questions.ai_explanation: Complete combustion converts the carbon atoms of a hydrocarbon into carbon dioxide and its hydrogen atoms into water. Excess oxygen supports complete rather than incomplete combustion.
questions.explanation: Complete combustion converts the carbon atoms of a hydrocarbon into carbon dioxide and its hydrogen atoms into water. Excess oxygen supports complete rather than incomplete combustion.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Cracking medicinal paraffin produces a gas that gives a pop with a lighted splint and an oily liquid that decolourises bromine solution. Which listed pair matches these observations?

questions.explanation: The gas that gives a pop with a lighted splint is hydrogen. The oily product decolourises bromine by addition at carbon–carbon unsaturation, consistent with an alkene from cracking. The matching pair is hydrogen and alkene.

questions.question: Terylene is formed from ethane-1,2-diol and benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid by which type of polymer-forming reaction?

questions.ai_explanation: A sieve separates particles by size. Smaller particles pass through its openings while larger particles are retained.

questions.question: Which listed substance gains mass by combining with oxygen when heated in air?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 50 cm³ of carbon monoxide reacts with 150 cm³ of air containing 20% oxygen by volume. Which reactant is in excess, comparing gas volumes at the same conditions?
questions.ai_explanation: The air supplies 150 × 0.20 = 30 cm³ oxygen. From 2CO + O₂ → 2CO₂, 50 cm³ CO requires 25 cm³ oxygen. Therefore oxygen is in excess by 5 cm³. Nitrogen is not a reactant here.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A fixed amount of ideal gas is initially at 0 °C and 9 atm. What is its final temperature if the pressure falls to 3 atm at constant volume? [0 °C = 273 K]
questions.ai_explanation: At constant volume for a fixed amount of ideal gas, P/T is constant. The initial temperature is 273 K. Thus T₂ = 273 × (3/9) = 91 K.
questions.explanation: At constant volume for a fixed amount of ideal gas, P/T is constant. The initial temperature is 273 K. Thus T₂ = 273 × (3/9) = 91 K.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Solubility curves for two solids P and Q both rise as temperature increases. P is more soluble than Q at each shown temperature. Which method uses this difference to separate their mixture into successive crystal fractions?
questions.ai_explanation: The solids have different solubilities at the same temperature. Controlled cooling and successive collection of crystals can separate them into fractions. This process is fractional crystallisation.
questions.explanation: The solids have different solubilities at the same temperature. Controlled cooling and successive collection of crystals can separate them into fractions. This process is fractional crystallisation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The ratio of initial to final pressure of a fixed amount of gas is 1:1.5. What is its final volume if its initial volume is 300 cm³ at the same temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: Boyle’s law gives P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ at constant temperature. Hence V₂ = (1/1.5) × 300 = 200 cm³. Higher pressure gives a smaller volume.
questions.explanation: Boyle’s law gives P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ at constant temperature. Hence V₂ = (1/1.5) × 300 = 200 cm³. Higher pressure gives a smaller volume.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) → MgCl₂(aq) + H₂(g). What mass of magnesium reacts completely with 250 cm³ of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ HCl? [Mg = 24]
questions.ai_explanation: The amount of HCl is 0.250 × 0.5 = 0.125 mol. Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ requires half as many moles of Mg: 0.0625 mol. With Mg = 24, the mass is 0.0625 × 24 = 1.5 g.
questions.explanation: The amount of HCl is 0.250 × 0.5 = 0.125 mol. Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ requires half as many moles of Mg: 0.0625 mol. With Mg = 24, the mass is 0.0625 × 24 = 1.5 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A gas sample has oxygen partial pressure 452 mmHg and total pressure 780 mmHg. What is the oxygen mole fraction?
questions.ai_explanation: Dalton’s law gives mole fraction = partial pressure / total pressure. For oxygen this is 452/780 = 0.579 to three decimal places.
questions.explanation: Dalton’s law gives mole fraction = partial pressure / total pressure. For oxygen this is 452/780 = 0.579 to three decimal places.

options.C: shape of the container they occupy

questions.question: In which sample do water molecules have the most disordered spatial arrangement?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Removing one 3s electron from each atom in one mole of gaseous sodium atoms requires about 496 kJ. What is this energy called?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which method can soften hard water?

questions.explanation: A suitable ion-exchange resin removes hardness-causing Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ ions by replacing them with ions such as Na⁺. Chlorination and aeration do not perform this exchange.

questions.question: Four positions in a periodic-table section are labelled: W is in Group I, period 3; X in Group IV, period 2; Y in Group VII, period 3; and Z in Group 0, period 2. Which element is least reactive?

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 0.25 mol HCl is dissolved and made up to 0.50 dm³. A 15.00 cm³ portion neutralises 12.50 cm³ of aqueous sodium carbonate completely. What is the carbonate concentration?

questions.question: Cu(IO₃)₂ has Ksp = 1.08 × 10⁻⁷. Assuming negligible reaction of its ions with water, what is its molar solubility in pure water?

questions.question: What charge is required to liberate 0.125 mol O₂ during electrolysis of dilute sodium chloride solution, assuming full current efficiency for oxygen evolution? [F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹]

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Current I deposits X g of a univalent metal in 40 minutes. What mass is deposited by current 2I in 10 minutes under the same conditions?
questions.ai_explanation: For the same metal and current efficiency, deposited mass is proportional to charge It. The second charge is (2I × 10)/(I × 40) = 1/2 of the first, so the deposited mass is X/2 g.
questions.explanation: For the same metal and current efficiency, deposited mass is proportional to charge It. The second charge is (2I × 10)/(I × 40) = 1/2 of the first, so the deposited mass is X/2 g.

questions.ai_explanation: The enthalpy change is H(products) − H(reactants). A negative value of −65.7 kJ mol⁻¹ means that the products have lower enthalpy and heat is released. It does not determine the reaction speed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which gas forms a white precipitate when passed into aqueous silver nitrate acidified with nitric acid?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen is used in oxyhydrogen flames for melting metals because it

options.A: Evolves a lot of heat when burnt

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A heated flask contains mixture Y. Gas passes from the flask through a drying vessel containing calcium oxide, then into an inverted gas jar labelled ammonia. What is mixture Y?
questions.ai_explanation: Heating ammonium chloride with calcium hydroxide releases ammonia: 2NH₄Cl + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCl₂ + 2NH₃ + 2H₂O. Calcium oxide dries the ammonia without reacting with it as an acidic drying agent would.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which properties make duralumin especially useful compared with its constituent metals?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed pair of reactive metals is extracted by electrolysis of suitable molten compounds?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed metal becomes passive in concentrated nitric acid?

questions.question: When excess ethanol is heated to 145 °C in the presence of concentrated H₂SO₄, the main organic product is
questions.ai_explanation: At about 140–145 °C with excess ethanol and concentrated sulfuric acid, intermolecular dehydration produces diethyl ether: 2C₂H₅OH → C₂H₅OC₂H₅ + H₂O. Higher temperatures favour ethene formation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: How many grams of bromine are required for complete addition to 5.2 g of but-1-en-3-yne? [C = 12, H = 1, Br = 80]
questions.ai_explanation: But-1-en-3-yne is CH₂=CH–C≡CH, with formula C₄H₄ and molar mass 52 g mol⁻¹. One C=C bond consumes one Br₂ and one C≡C consumes two Br₂ on full addition. Thus 5.2/52 × 3 × 160 = 48.0 g bromine is required.
questions.explanation: But-1-en-3-yne is CH₂=CH–C≡CH, with formula C₄H₄ and molar mass 52 g mol⁻¹. One C=C bond consumes one Br₂ and one C≡C consumes two Br₂ on full addition. Thus 5.2/52 × 3 × 160 = 48.0 g bromine is required.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Polyvinyl chloride is commonly used to produce

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When the two terminal alkyl groups of ethyl ethanoate are interchanged, the compound formed is
questions.ai_explanation: Ethyl ethanoate is CH₃–C(=O)–O–C₂H₅. Swapping the terminal methyl and ethyl groups gives C₂H₅–C(=O)–O–CH₃. The alcohol-derived group is methyl and the acid-derived part has three carbons, so the ester is methyl propanoate.

questions.subject: chemistry

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In HCl(aq) + H₂O(l) → H₃O⁺(aq) + Cl⁻(aq), what is Cl⁻ in relation to HCl?

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Using the ideal concentration model at 25 °C, what is the pOH of 0.25 mol dm⁻³ hydrochloric acid?
questions.ai_explanation: For fully dissociated HCl, [H⁺] = 0.25 mol dm⁻³. Thus pH = −log₁₀(0.25) = 0.602 and, at 25 °C in the ideal dilute-solution model, pOH = 14.00 − 0.602 = 13.40.

questions.question: Complete the reduction half-equation: MnO₄⁻(aq) + 8H⁺(aq) + Y → Mn²⁺(aq) + 4H₂O(l). What is Y?
questions.ai_explanation: Manganese changes from +7 in MnO₄⁻ to +2, gaining five electrons. The balanced half-equation is MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, with equal charge and atoms on both sides.

questions.question: Which rate-versus-concentration plot represents a zero-order reaction?
