questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Complete catalytic hydrogenation of benzene produces
questions.ai_explanation: Complete catalytic hydrogenation adds three molecules of H₂ to each benzene molecule: C₆H₆ + 3H₂ → C₆H₁₂. The saturated ring product is cyclohexane.
questions.explanation: Complete catalytic hydrogenation adds three molecules of H₂ to each benzene molecule: C₆H₆ + 3H₂ → C₆H₁₂. The saturated ring product is cyclohexane.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When chlorine is passed into water and the resulting chlorine water is exposed to sunlight, the final products are
questions.ai_explanation: Chlorine initially reacts with water to form HCl and HClO. Sunlight decomposes hypochlorous acid: 2HClO → 2HCl + O₂. The overall products are hydrochloric acid and oxygen.
questions.explanation: Chlorine initially reacts with water to form HCl and HClO. Sunlight decomposes hypochlorous acid: 2HClO → 2HCl + O₂. The overall products are hydrochloric acid and oxygen.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which pair consists of structural isomers?
questions.ai_explanation: But-1-ene and but-2-ene both have molecular formula C₄H₈ but differ in double-bond position. The other pairs have different molecular formulas and are not isomers.
questions.explanation: But-1-ene and but-2-ene both have molecular formula C₄H₈ but differ in double-bond position. The other pairs have different molecular formulas and are not isomers.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: During vulcanisation of rubber, sulfur is added to
questions.ai_explanation: Sulfur forms cross-links between rubber chains. These links restrict chain slippage and improve the useful elastic and mechanical properties of rubber.
questions.explanation: Sulfur forms cross-links between rubber chains. These links restrict chain slippage and improve the useful elastic and mechanical properties of rubber.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When sodium reacts with water, the resulting solution is
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium reacts with water to give sodium hydroxide and hydrogen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Hydroxide ions make the resulting solution alkaline.
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts with water to give sodium hydroxide and hydrogen: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. Hydroxide ions make the resulting solution alkaline.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The condensed general formula for alkanals is
questions.ai_explanation: Alkanals contain a terminal –CHO group, so their condensed general formula is RCHO. R is an alkyl group, or hydrogen in methanal.
questions.explanation: Alkanals contain a terminal –CHO group, so their condensed general formula is RCHO. R is an alkyl group, or hydrogen in methanal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed metal gives a brick-red flame?
questions.ai_explanation: Calcium gives a brick-red flame in the characteristic flame test. Magnesium burns with an intense white light, while sodium gives a strong yellow flame.
questions.explanation: Calcium gives a brick-red flame in the characteristic flame test. Magnesium burns with an intense white light, while sodium gives a strong yellow flame.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which gas is best collected by downward displacement of air?
questions.ai_explanation: Ammonia is less dense than air and very soluble in water. It rises into an inverted gas jar and pushes air downwards, so downward displacement of air is suitable.
questions.explanation: Ammonia is less dense than air and very soluble in water. It rises into an inverted gas jar and pushes air downwards, so downward displacement of air is suitable.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The principal gangue impurity removed by lime in the conventional blast-furnace extraction of iron is
questions.ai_explanation: Silica, SiO₂, is a common gangue impurity in iron ore. Calcium oxide from limestone reacts with it to form calcium silicate slag, removing it from the iron.
questions.explanation: Silica, SiO₂, is a common gangue impurity in iron ore. Calcium oxide from limestone reacts with it to form calcium silicate slag, removing it from the iron.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the percentage by mass of oxygen in Al₂(SO₄)₃·2H₂O? [Al = 27, S = 32, H = 1, O = 16]
questions.ai_explanation: The formula contains 2 Al, 3 S, 14 O and 4 H atoms. Its molar mass is 54 + 96 + 224 + 4 = 378 g mol⁻¹. Oxygen contributes 224 g, so its percentage is 224/378 × 100 = 59.26% to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The formula contains 2 Al, 3 S, 14 O and 4 H atoms. Its molar mass is 54 + 96 + 224 + 4 = 378 g mol⁻¹. Oxygen contributes 224 g, so its percentage is 224/378 × 100 = 59.26% to two decimal places.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which gas forms the complex responsible for the brown colour in the brown-ring test?
questions.ai_explanation: Nitric oxide, NO, binds to iron in the nitrosyl complex responsible for the brown ring. The colour belongs to the complex; free NO gas is colourless.
questions.explanation: Nitric oxide, NO, binds to iron in the nitrosyl complex responsible for the brown ring. The colour belongs to the complex; free NO gas is colourless.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which aqueous solution forms a precipitate when a small amount of NaOH solution is added?
questions.ai_explanation: Adding a limited amount of hydroxide to aluminium chloride forms white Al(OH)₃: Al³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Al(OH)₃(s). The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric.
questions.explanation: Adding a limited amount of hydroxide to aluminium chloride forms white Al(OH)₃: Al³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Al(OH)₃(s). The precipitate dissolves in excess NaOH because aluminium hydroxide is amphoteric.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The reaction of an alkene with hydrogen in the presence of a catalyst is
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen adds across the alkene C=C bond in the presence of a suitable catalyst. The carbon skeleton remains intact and a saturated alkane forms, so this is an addition reaction.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen adds across the alkene C=C bond in the presence of a suitable catalyst. The carbon skeleton remains intact and a saturated alkane forms, so this is an addition reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The intermediate formed when ethanol is progressively oxidised to ethanoic acid using acidified potassium dichromate is
questions.ai_explanation: Ethanol first oxidises to ethanal, CH₃CHO. Further oxidation converts the aldehyde group into the carboxylic acid group of ethanoic acid.
questions.explanation: Ethanol first oxidises to ethanal, CH₃CHO. Further oxidation converts the aldehyde group into the carboxylic acid group of ethanoic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃ is a
questions.ai_explanation: In CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃, the carbon bearing OH is bonded to two other carbon atoms and one hydrogen. It is therefore a secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol.
questions.explanation: In CH₃CH₂CH(OH)CH₃, the carbon bearing OH is bonded to two other carbon atoms and one hydrogen. It is therefore a secondary alcohol, butan-2-ol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is the specific name for boiling fat with aqueous caustic soda to produce soap?
questions.ai_explanation: Boiling a fat with aqueous sodium hydroxide breaks its ester bonds to form glycerol and sodium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps. This specific alkaline hydrolysis is called saponification.
questions.explanation: Boiling a fat with aqueous sodium hydroxide breaks its ester bonds to form glycerol and sodium salts of fatty acids, which are soaps. This specific alkaline hydrolysis is called saponification.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ordinary soda-lime glass is manufactured from silica, CaCO₃ and
questions.ai_explanation: Soda-lime glass is made using silica, limestone and sodium carbonate. Sodium carbonate supplies sodium oxide in the melt and acts as a flux, lowering the temperature needed to process silica.
questions.explanation: Soda-lime glass is made using silica, limestone and sodium carbonate. Sodium carbonate supplies sodium oxide in the melt and acts as a flux, lowering the temperature needed to process silica.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed element is especially noted for extensive catenation into long chains and rings?
questions.ai_explanation: Carbon forms strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, supporting extensive chains, branched structures and rings. This extensive catenation is central to organic chemistry.
questions.explanation: Carbon forms strong covalent bonds with other carbon atoms, supporting extensive chains, branched structures and rings. This extensive catenation is central to organic chemistry.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol can be produced from starch by
questions.ai_explanation: Starch is first hydrolysed into fermentable sugars. Yeast can then convert those sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Distillation separates ethanol after production but does not convert starch into ethanol.
questions.explanation: Starch is first hydrolysed into fermentable sugars. Yeast can then convert those sugars into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Distillation separates ethanol after production but does not convert starch into ethanol.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Hydrogen is readily released when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium is sufficiently reactive to release hydrogen from aqueous hydrochloric acid, producing sodium chloride. Silver, gold and copper do not displace hydrogen from dilute non-oxidising hydrochloric acid under ordinary conditions.
questions.explanation: Sodium is sufficiently reactive to release hydrogen from aqueous hydrochloric acid, producing sodium chloride. Silver, gold and copper do not displace hydrogen from dilute non-oxidising hydrochloric acid under ordinary conditions.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement about a proton is correct?

options.B: Its mass is one-twelfth the molar mass of carbon
options.C: Its mass is approximately 1840 times the mass of an electron
options.D: The total mass of the protons in any nucleus is always half its nuclear mass

questions.ai_explanation: A proton is about 1836 times as massive as an electron, often rounded to 1840 in school calculations. Its mass is about 1.67 × 10⁻²⁴ g. A molar mass describes one mole, not one particle, and nuclei do not all have equal numbers of protons and neutrons.
questions.explanation: A proton is about 1836 times as massive as an electron, often rounded to 1840 in school calculations. Its mass is about 1.67 × 10⁻²⁴ g. A molar mass describes one mole, not one particle, and nuclei do not all have equal numbers of protons and neutrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In the beta-minus decay ¹⁴₆C → X + β⁻, which nuclide is X?
questions.ai_explanation: In beta-minus decay a neutron changes into a proton, so atomic number increases by one while mass number stays the same. Carbon-14, with atomic number 6, becomes nitrogen-14 with atomic number 7.
questions.explanation: In beta-minus decay a neutron changes into a proton, so atomic number increases by one while mass number stays the same. Carbon-14, with atomic number 6, becomes nitrogen-14 with atomic number 7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which chloride has the least ionic character?
questions.ai_explanation: Al³⁺ has high charge and small size, giving strong polarising power. It distorts the chloride electron cloud, increasing covalent character; AlCl₃ is therefore the least ionic of these choices.
questions.explanation: Al³⁺ has high charge and small size, giving strong polarising power. It distorts the chloride electron cloud, increasing covalent character; AlCl₃ is therefore the least ionic of these choices.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Processes that return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere include
questions.ai_explanation: Respiration, aerobic decomposition and combustion release carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis instead takes up CO₂, and transpiration chiefly releases water vapour.
questions.explanation: Respiration, aerobic decomposition and combustion release carbon dioxide. Photosynthesis instead takes up CO₂, and transpiration chiefly releases water vapour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which Dalton postulate is retained in the modern description of stoichiometric compounds?

options.A: All elements consist of indivisible particles
options.B: Atoms of different elements combine in simple whole-number ratios
options.C: Atoms can never be created or destroyed in any process
options.D: All atoms of the same element are exactly alike

questions.ai_explanation: Atoms combine in whole-number ratios in the formulas of stoichiometric compounds. Atoms have subatomic structure, isotopes of an element need not be identical in mass, and nuclear processes can transform atoms, so those absolute older claims require revision.
questions.explanation: Atoms combine in whole-number ratios in the formulas of stoichiometric compounds. Atoms have subatomic structure, isotopes of an element need not be identical in mass, and nuclear processes can transform atoms, so those absolute older claims require revision.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A non-reacting ideal-gas mixture contains 0.75 mol cyclopropane and 0.66 mol oxygen at total pressure 0.7 atm. What is the partial pressure of oxygen?
questions.ai_explanation: The oxygen mole fraction is 0.66/(0.75 + 0.66) = 0.4681. Dalton’s law gives p(O₂) = 0.4681 × 0.7 = 0.3277 atm, or 0.33 atm.
questions.explanation: The oxygen mole fraction is 0.66/(0.75 + 0.66) = 0.4681. Dalton’s law gives p(O₂) = 0.4681 × 0.7 = 0.3277 atm, or 0.33 atm.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When H₂S reduces aqueous iron(III) chloride, the resulting iron-ion solution is
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen sulfide reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺, whose aqueous solution is pale green: 2Fe³⁺ + H₂S → 2Fe²⁺ + S + 2H⁺. Sulfur also separates as a solid.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen sulfide reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺, whose aqueous solution is pale green: 2Fe³⁺ + H₂S → 2Fe²⁺ + S + 2H⁺. Sulfur also separates as a solid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which condition specifically indicates chemical equilibrium at fixed temperature and pressure? Here ΔᵣG is the reaction Gibbs energy at the current composition.
questions.ai_explanation: At equilibrium, the reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG is zero, so neither direction has a thermodynamic driving force. This does not require the standard reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG° to be zero.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, the reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG is zero, so neither direction has a thermodynamic driving force. This does not require the standard reaction Gibbs energy ΔᵣG° to be zero.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For Cu₂S(s) + O₂(g) → 2Cu(s) + SO₂(g), how does copper’s oxidation number change?
questions.ai_explanation: Sulfide has oxidation number −2 in Cu₂S, so each copper is +1. Elemental copper has oxidation number 0, giving the change +1 → 0.
questions.explanation: Sulfide has oxidation number −2 in Cu₂S, so each copper is +1. Elemental copper has oxidation number 0, giving the change +1 → 0.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Electrolysis of dilute aqueous sodium hydroxide using platinum electrodes produces
questions.ai_explanation: With inert platinum electrodes, water is reduced to hydrogen at the cathode and hydroxide is oxidised to oxygen at the anode. The net change is 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.
questions.explanation: With inert platinum electrodes, water is reduced to hydrogen at the cathode and hydroxide is oxidised to oxygen at the anode. The net change is 2H₂O → 2H₂ + O₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For PCl₅(g) ⇌ PCl₃(g) + Cl₂(g), which statement describes the equilibrium shift when pressure is decreased by expansion at fixed temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole on the reactant side. Expansion at fixed temperature lowers pressure and favours the products, increasing the equilibrium amount of PCl₃.
questions.explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole on the reactant side. Expansion at fixed temperature lowers pressure and favours the products, increasing the equilibrium amount of PCl₃.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The Arrhenius equation relates a reaction’s rate constant to temperature and its
questions.ai_explanation: The Arrhenius equation is k = A exp(−Eₐ/RT). It relates the rate constant to activation energy and temperature, with A the pre-exponential factor. At fixed A and T, a lower activation energy gives a larger rate constant.
questions.explanation: The Arrhenius equation is k = A exp(−Eₐ/RT). It relates the rate constant to activation energy and temperature, with A the pre-exponential factor. At fixed A and T, a lower activation energy gives a larger rate constant.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which description gives the thermal effect when NaOH flakes dissolve in water?
questions.ai_explanation: Dissolving sodium hydroxide releases heat overall because hydration of its ions releases more energy than is needed to separate the solid lattice. The solution warms, so the change is exothermic.
questions.explanation: Dissolving sodium hydroxide releases heat overall because hydration of its ions releases more energy than is needed to separate the solid lattice. The solution warms, so the change is exothermic.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Water vapour changes anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride from
questions.ai_explanation: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue. On taking up water it forms hydrated species that appear pink, producing the blue-to-pink change used in a water test.
questions.explanation: Anhydrous cobalt(II) chloride is blue. On taking up water it forms hydrated species that appear pink, producing the blue-to-pink change used in a water test.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: At 20 °C, a salt of molar mass 101 g mol⁻¹ has solubility 0.34 mol dm⁻³. If 3.40 g dissolves in 250 cm³ of water with negligible volume change, the solution is
questions.ai_explanation: The amount is 3.40/101 = 0.0337 mol. With negligible volume change, concentration is 0.0337/0.250 = 0.135 mol dm⁻³, below the solubility of 0.34 mol dm⁻³. More salt can dissolve, so the solution is unsaturated.
questions.explanation: The amount is 3.40/101 = 0.0337 mol. With negligible volume change, concentration is 0.0337/0.250 = 0.135 mol dm⁻³, below the solubility of 0.34 mol dm⁻³. More salt can dissolve, so the solution is unsaturated.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: 25 cm³ of 0.2 mol dm⁻³ Na₂CO₃ requires 20 cm³ of HCl for complete neutralisation. What is the HCl concentration?
questions.ai_explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate amount is 0.025 × 0.2 = 0.005 mol, requiring 0.010 mol HCl. The acid concentration is 0.010/0.020 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.
questions.explanation: Na₂CO₃ + 2HCl → 2NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. The carbonate amount is 0.025 × 0.2 = 0.005 mol, requiring 0.010 mol HCl. The acid concentration is 0.010/0.020 = 0.50 mol dm⁻³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When a hydrated salt loses water of crystallisation on exposure to air, the process is called
questions.ai_explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. Deliquescence instead involves absorbing moisture until the solid dissolves.
questions.explanation: Efflorescence is the loss of water of crystallisation from a hydrated salt on exposure to air. Deliquescence instead involves absorbing moisture until the solid dissolves.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Three drops of 1.0 mol dm⁻³ NaOH are added to 20 cm³ of an aqueous solution at pH 8.4. The resulting pH will be

options.D: Close to that of pure water

questions.ai_explanation: Adding concentrated sodium hydroxide increases the hydroxide concentration and decreases the hydrogen-ion concentration. The resulting pH is greater than 8.4.
questions.explanation: Adding concentrated sodium hydroxide increases the hydroxide concentration and decreases the hydrogen-ion concentration. The resulting pH is greater than 8.4.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which interaction chiefly explains why a small alcohol such as ethanol mixes readily with water?
questions.ai_explanation: The OH group in a small alcohol such as ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water. This favours mixing; solubility decreases as the non-polar carbon chain becomes longer.
questions.explanation: The OH group in a small alcohol such as ethanol can form hydrogen bonds with water. This favours mixing; solubility decreases as the non-polar carbon chain becomes longer.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Calcium carbonate scale formed when temporary hard water is boiled comes from dissolved
questions.ai_explanation: On heating, dissolved calcium hydrogencarbonate decomposes: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃(s) + CO₂ + H₂O. Insoluble calcium carbonate coats the kettle as scale.
questions.explanation: On heating, dissolved calcium hydrogencarbonate decomposes: Ca(HCO₃)₂ → CaCO₃(s) + CO₂ + H₂O. Insoluble calcium carbonate coats the kettle as scale.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In 3Cu + pHNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + xNO, what are p and x respectively?
questions.ai_explanation: Three copper atoms lose six electrons in total. Two nitrate nitrogen atoms each gain three electrons to form NO; six further nitrate groups remain with copper. Balancing H and O gives 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + 2NO.
questions.explanation: Three copper atoms lose six electrons in total. Two nitrate nitrogen atoms each gain three electrons to form NO; six further nitrate groups remain with copper. Balancing H and O gives 3Cu + 8HNO₃ → 3Cu(NO₃)₂ + 4H₂O + 2NO.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Neon and the heavier noble gases owe their low reactivity largely to their
questions.ai_explanation: Neon and the heavier noble gases have eight outer-shell electrons, a stable octet. Helium is a separate case with its first shell filled by two electrons.
questions.explanation: Neon and the heavier noble gases have eight outer-shell electrons, a stable octet. Helium is a separate case with its first shell filled by two electrons.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: According to kinetic theory, increasing absolute temperature causes average kinetic energy of gas particles to
questions.ai_explanation: Mean translational kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to absolute temperature: average Eₖ = 3kT/2. Increasing temperature therefore increases their average kinetic energy.
questions.explanation: Mean translational kinetic energy of gas particles is proportional to absolute temperature: average Eₖ = 3kT/2. Increasing temperature therefore increases their average kinetic energy.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: When cathode rays are deflected onto the electrode of an electrometer, the instrument becomes
questions.ai_explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. Collection of these electrons by the electrometer electrode adds negative charge.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays are streams of electrons. Collection of these electrons by the electrometer electrode adds negative charge.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed interaction is ordinarily the weakest individual attraction?
questions.ai_explanation: Van der Waals interactions are generally much weaker individually than ordinary ionic or covalent bonds. Coordinate covalent bonds are also covalent bonds.
questions.explanation: Van der Waals interactions are generally much weaker individually than ordinary ionic or covalent bonds. Coordinate covalent bonds are also covalent bonds.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which ion acts as an acid in water?
questions.ai_explanation: Hydronium, H₃O⁺, donates a proton in aqueous acid-base reactions. K⁺ and NO₃⁻ do not appreciably acidify water, while S²⁻ acts as a base.
questions.explanation: Hydronium, H₃O⁺, donates a proton in aqueous acid-base reactions. K⁺ and NO₃⁻ do not appreciably acidify water, while S²⁻ acts as a base.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which method can biologically help decontaminate farmland affected by crude-oil spillage?
questions.ai_explanation: Suitable aerobic bacteria break down some petroleum hydrocarbons in the presence of oxygen. This bioremediation requires appropriate conditions and does not instantly remove every oil component.
questions.explanation: Suitable aerobic bacteria break down some petroleum hydrocarbons in the presence of oxygen. This bioremediation requires appropriate conditions and does not instantly remove every oil component.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For an equilibrium whose forward reaction has ΔH > 0, which temperature change favours the forward equilibrium direction?
questions.ai_explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic when ΔH is positive. Raising temperature favours the heat-absorbing direction and shifts equilibrium towards products.
questions.explanation: The forward reaction is endothermic when ΔH is positive. Raising temperature favours the heat-absorbing direction and shifts equilibrium towards products.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The defining feature of an anode reaction is that
questions.ai_explanation: Oxidation occurs at the anode: a species loses electrons. An anode may dissolve if it is an active metal, but dissolution is not required for every anode reaction.
questions.explanation: Oxidation occurs at the anode: a species loses electrons. An anode may dissolve if it is an active metal, but dissolution is not required for every anode reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which quantity changes when a catalyst provides an alternative pathway?
questions.ai_explanation: A catalyst provides a pathway with lower activation energy. It does not alter the energies of starting reactants and final products, so reaction enthalpy is unchanged.
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides a pathway with lower activation energy. It does not alter the energies of starting reactants and final products, so reaction enthalpy is unchanged.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: If Y is an oxidizing agent that reacts with a reducing agent, Z, which of the following is correct?
questions.ai_explanation: An oxidising agent accepts electrons and is reduced. Thus Y is reduced while reducing agent Z loses electrons and is oxidised.
questions.explanation: An oxidising agent accepts electrons and is reduced. Thus Y is reduced while reducing agent Z loses electrons and is oxidised.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In electrolysis of concentrated aqueous NaCl with inert electrodes, which pair represents cathode and anode discharge respectively in introductory ion-discharge notation?
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen forms at the cathode and chlorine at the anode. Introductory ion-discharge notation describes these as H⁺ and Cl⁻ discharge. The cathode process is more directly written 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen forms at the cathode and chlorine at the anode. Introductory ion-discharge notation describes these as H⁺ and Cl⁻ discharge. The cathode process is more directly written 2H₂O + 2e⁻ → H₂ + 2OH⁻.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For CO(g) + H₂O(g) → CO₂(g) + H₂(g), calculate ΔH° using formation enthalpies CO₂(g) = −394, H₂O(g) = −242 and CO(g) = −110 kJ mol⁻¹.
questions.ai_explanation: Use products minus reactants: ΔH° = [−394 + 0] − [−110 + (−242)] = −42 kJ mol⁻¹. Hydrogen in its standard elemental state has zero standard enthalpy of formation.
questions.explanation: Use products minus reactants: ΔH° = [−394 + 0] − [−110 + (−242)] = −42 kJ mol⁻¹. Hydrogen in its standard elemental state has zero standard enthalpy of formation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed sample conducts electricity through mobile ions under the stated conditions?
questions.ai_explanation: Sodium acetate solution contains mobile Na⁺ and CH₃COO⁻ ions. Solid KOH has ions fixed in a lattice; mercury conducts through electrons rather than electrolytic ion movement.
questions.explanation: Sodium acetate solution contains mobile Na⁺ and CH₃COO⁻ ions. Solid KOH has ions fixed in a lattice; mercury conducts through electrons rather than electrolytic ion movement.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Many characteristic transition-metal properties arise from partly filled subshells in their atoms or ions of type
questions.ai_explanation: Many transition-metal properties arise from incompletely filled d subshells in their atoms or common ions. These states help explain variable oxidation states and many coloured complexes.
questions.explanation: Many transition-metal properties arise from incompletely filled d subshells in their atoms or common ions. These states help explain variable oxidation states and many coloured complexes.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which statement is true of sulfur(IV) oxide, SO₂?

options.A: It forms sulfuric acid directly with water
options.D: It gives a white precipitate with acidified barium chloride

questions.ai_explanation: SO₂ is an acidic oxide, conventionally described as the anhydride of sulfurous acid. It acidifies water and is pungent rather than odourless. Dissolving it in water does not directly produce sulfuric acid.
questions.explanation: SO₂ is an acidic oxide, conventionally described as the anhydride of sulfurous acid. It acidifies water and is pungent rather than odourless. Dissolving it in water does not directly produce sulfuric acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which salt solution forms a precipitate with aqueous ammonia that dissolves in excess ammonia?
questions.ai_explanation: A little aqueous ammonia produces blue Cu(OH)₂ from Cu²⁺. Excess ammonia dissolves it by forming a deep-blue soluble copper-ammonia complex, commonly written [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺.
questions.explanation: A little aqueous ammonia produces blue Cu(OH)₂ from Cu²⁺. Excess ammonia dissolves it by forming a deep-blue soluble copper-ammonia complex, commonly written [Cu(NH₃)₄(H₂O)₂]²⁺.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What initial colour does chlorine produce on damp starch-iodide paper?
questions.ai_explanation: Chlorine oxidises iodide to iodine: Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → I₂ + 2Cl⁻. Liberated iodine forms a dark-blue complex with starch, giving the characteristic initial colour.
questions.explanation: Chlorine oxidises iodide to iodine: Cl₂ + 2I⁻ → I₂ + 2Cl⁻. Liberated iodine forms a dark-blue complex with starch, giving the characteristic initial colour.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Converting molten iron to steel in the basic oxygen process chiefly removes impurities by
questions.ai_explanation: In basic oxygen steelmaking, oxygen oxidises excess carbon and other impurities in molten iron. Carbon leaves mainly as gases, while suitable oxides enter the slag.
questions.explanation: In basic oxygen steelmaking, oxygen oxidises excess carbon and other impurities in molten iron. Carbon leaves mainly as gases, while suitable oxides enter the slag.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ethene reacts with hydrogen bromide to form
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen bromide adds across ethene’s double bond: CH₂=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CH₂Br. Both ethene carbons are equivalent, so no regioselectivity distinction is needed.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bromide adds across ethene’s double bond: CH₂=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CH₂Br. Both ethene carbons are equivalent, so no regioselectivity distinction is needed.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For a simple monosaccharide represented by (CH₂O)ₙ, what is the C:H:O atom ratio?
questions.ai_explanation: Simple monosaccharides such as glucose have the general formula (CH₂O)ₙ, giving C:H:O = 1:2:1. This ratio is not universal for every carbohydrate; polysaccharide formation removes water.
questions.explanation: Simple monosaccharides such as glucose have the general formula (CH₂O)ₙ, giving C:H:O = 1:2:1. This ratio is not universal for every carbohydrate; polysaccharide formation removes water.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The condensed structural formula of ethyl butanoate is
questions.ai_explanation: Butanoate contributes CH₃CH₂CH₂COO–, written C₃H₇COO–. The ethyl group attached through oxygen is C₂H₅, so ethyl butanoate is C₃H₇COOC₂H₅.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which reaction type is characteristic of benzene?
questions.ai_explanation: Benzene characteristically undergoes electrophilic substitution, replacing a ring hydrogen while restoring its aromatic electron system. Addition is possible under more forcing conditions but is not its characteristic reaction.
questions.explanation: Benzene characteristically undergoes electrophilic substitution, replacing a ring hydrogen while restoring its aromatic electron system. Addition is possible under more forcing conditions but is not its characteristic reaction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: On heating under reflux with excess acidified K₂Cr₂O₇, ethanol forms
questions.ai_explanation: Excess acidified dichromate oxidises ethanol through ethanal to ethanoic acid. Heating under reflux retains volatile material and allows oxidation to the carboxylic acid.
questions.explanation: Excess acidified dichromate oxidises ethanol through ethanal to ethanoic acid. Heating under reflux retains volatile material and allows oxidation to the carboxylic acid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: For N₂O₄(g) ⇌ 2NO₂(g), which change at fixed temperature favours more product?

options.A: A decrease in pressure by expansion
options.C: An increase in pressure by compression

questions.ai_explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole of N₂O₄. Decreasing pressure by expansion at fixed temperature favours the side with more gas molecules, producing more NO₂.
questions.explanation: The product side has two moles of gas for each mole of N₂O₄. Decreasing pressure by expansion at fixed temperature favours the side with more gas molecules, producing more NO₂.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What is chlorine’s oxidation state in HClO₄?
questions.ai_explanation: In neutral HClO₄, hydrogen is +1 and four oxygen atoms total −8. Therefore 1 + x − 8 = 0, so chlorine is +7.
questions.explanation: In neutral HClO₄, hydrogen is +1 and four oxygen atoms total −8. Therefore 1 + x − 8 = 0, so chlorine is +7.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which hydrogen halide has the highest standard molar entropy as a gas at 298.15 K?
questions.ai_explanation: At 298.15 K, standard molar gas entropies are approximately HF 173.8, HCl 186.9, HBr 198.7 and HI 206.6 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. HI has the largest value in this series.
questions.explanation: At 298.15 K, standard molar gas entropies are approximately HF 173.8, HCl 186.9, HBr 198.7 and HI 206.6 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹. HI has the largest value in this series.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What mass of silver is deposited by a 10 A current through an Ag⁺ solution for 4830 s, at 100% current efficiency? [Ag = 108 g mol⁻¹; F = 96,500 C mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: For Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, one mole of electrons deposits one mole of silver. Q = It = 10 × 4830 = 48,300 C. Mass = 48,300/96,500 × 108 = 54.055 g, or 54.1 g to one decimal place.
questions.explanation: For Ag⁺ + e⁻ → Ag, one mole of electrons deposits one mole of silver. Q = It = 10 × 4830 = 48,300 C. Mass = 48,300/96,500 × 108 = 54.055 g, or 54.1 g to one decimal place.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which ideal-gas equilibrium does not shift when volume decreases at fixed temperature?
questions.ai_explanation: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI has two moles of gas on each side. Compression at fixed temperature scales numerator and denominator of its pressure quotient equally, so it causes no equilibrium shift in the ideal-gas approximation.
questions.explanation: H₂ + I₂ ⇌ 2HI has two moles of gas on each side. Compression at fixed temperature scales numerator and denominator of its pressure quotient equally, so it causes no equilibrium shift in the ideal-gas approximation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: In ZnO + CO → Zn + CO₂, zinc has been
questions.ai_explanation: Zinc is +2 in ZnO and 0 in elemental Zn. The decrease in oxidation number means zinc is reduced; carbon monoxide is oxidised to carbon dioxide.
questions.explanation: Zinc is +2 in ZnO and 0 in elemental Zn. The decrease in oxidation number means zinc is reduced; carbon monoxide is oxidised to carbon dioxide.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of CO₂ at s.t.p. is formed when 2 g of CaCO₃ reacts completely with excess HCl? [Ca = 40, C = 12, O = 16; molar gas volume = 22.4 dm³ mol⁻¹]
questions.ai_explanation: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + CO₂ + H₂O. The carbonate molar mass is 100 g mol⁻¹, so 2 g gives 0.020 mol CO₂. Volume = 0.020 × 22.4 = 0.448 dm³ = 448 cm³.
questions.explanation: CaCO₃ + 2HCl → CaCl₂ + CO₂ + H₂O. The carbonate molar mass is 100 g mol⁻¹, so 2 g gives 0.020 mol CO₂. Volume = 0.020 × 22.4 = 0.448 dm³ = 448 cm³.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A solid changes directly into gas on heating without becoming liquid. This process is
questions.ai_explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through the liquid state. Evaporation begins with a liquid, while crystallisation forms a solid.
questions.explanation: Sublimation is the direct change from solid to gas without passing through the liquid state. Evaporation begins with a liquid, while crystallisation forms a solid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What mass of CuO reacts completely with 4.9 g of H₂SO₄? [Cu = 64, O = 16, S = 32, H = 1]
questions.ai_explanation: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O is a 1:1 reaction. The acid amount is 4.9/98 = 0.050 mol. The required CuO mass is 0.050 × 80 = 4.0 g.
questions.explanation: CuO + H₂SO₄ → CuSO₄ + H₂O is a 1:1 reaction. The acid amount is 4.9/98 = 0.050 mol. The required CuO mass is 0.050 × 80 = 4.0 g.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The general formula of an acyclic saturated alkyl group is
questions.ai_explanation: An acyclic saturated alkyl group is formed by removing one hydrogen from an alkane, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Its formula is therefore CₙH₂ₙ₊₁–.
questions.explanation: An acyclic saturated alkyl group is formed by removing one hydrogen from an alkane, CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. Its formula is therefore CₙH₂ₙ₊₁–.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Ethanol is heated with concentrated H₂SO₄ at 180 °C. Which organic product forms?
questions.ai_explanation: Concentrated sulfuric acid at about 180 °C dehydrates ethanol: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O. The product is ethene.
questions.explanation: Concentrated sulfuric acid at about 180 °C dehydrates ethanol: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O. The product is ethene.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: During soap production, concentrated NaCl solution is added to
questions.ai_explanation: Concentrated sodium chloride lowers the solubility of sodium soaps in the aqueous mixture, allowing soap to separate. This separation is called salting out.
questions.explanation: Concentrated sodium chloride lowers the solubility of sodium soaps in the aqueous mixture, allowing soap to separate. This separation is called salting out.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: An oxyacetylene flame is useful for welding iron because it

options.A: Releases a large amount of heat during combustion
options.B: Dissociates to produce carbon dioxide and oxygen
options.C: Makes the metal solidify very quickly
options.D: Combines with oxygen to give a pop sound

questions.ai_explanation: Acetylene burns in oxygen with a concentrated, high-temperature flame. The heat can melt the metal locally so a weld can form.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which listed structure has molecular formula C₅H₁₂?
questions.ai_explanation: 2-Methylbutane has five carbon atoms and molecular formula C₅H₁₂. Butane and 2-methylpropane have only four carbons; the structure labelled 2-ethylbutane has six.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Alcohol + carboxylic acid ⇌ ester + water. What is the reverse reaction called?
questions.ai_explanation: In the reverse direction, an ester reacts with water to form an alcohol and a carboxylic acid. This is ester hydrolysis. Alkaline hydrolysis producing a carboxylate salt is called saponification.
questions.explanation: In the reverse direction, an ester reacts with water to form an alcohol and a carboxylic acid. This is ester hydrolysis. Alkaline hydrolysis producing a carboxylate salt is called saponification.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The transformation CH₃COOH(g) → CH₄(g) + CO₂(g) is classified as
questions.ai_explanation: The products contain carbon dioxide and a hydrocarbon with one fewer carbon atom than the acid. Removal of the carboxyl group as CO₂ is decarboxylation.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which soil condition commonly increases the leaching of many metal ions into groundwater?
questions.ai_explanation: Acidic conditions often increase dissolution and mobility of metal-containing minerals. This can allow metal ions to leach through soil and contaminate groundwater.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which compound is a normal salt rather than an acid salt?
questions.ai_explanation: A normal salt contains no replaceable acidic hydrogen from incomplete neutralisation. Na₂CO₃ is the fully neutralised sodium salt of carbonic acid; NaHCO₃, NaHSO₄ and NaHS are acid salts. Normal salt does not mean its solution has neutral pH.
questions.explanation: A normal salt contains no replaceable acidic hydrogen from incomplete neutralisation. Na₂CO₃ is the fully neutralised sodium salt of carbonic acid; NaHCO₃, NaHSO₄ and NaHS are acid salts. Normal salt does not mean its solution has neutral pH.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: What volume of 0.5 mol dm⁻³ H₂SO₄ exactly neutralises 20 cm³ of 0.1 mol dm⁻³ NaOH?
questions.ai_explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. NaOH amount = 0.020 × 0.1 = 0.0020 mol, requiring 0.0010 mol acid. Volume = 0.0010/0.5 = 0.0020 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.
questions.explanation: H₂SO₄ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₄ + 2H₂O. NaOH amount = 0.020 × 0.1 = 0.0020 mol, requiring 0.0010 mol acid. Volume = 0.0010/0.5 = 0.0020 dm³ = 2.0 cm³.

questions.question: The small amount of calcium sulfate that dissolves in water forms a
questions.ai_explanation: The dissolved portion of calcium sulfate exists as dispersed ions, forming a true solution. Its low solubility limits how much dissolves; it does not make the dissolved portion a colloid.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Gas molecules do not maintain a regular fixed arrangement chiefly because they

options.C: Have weak attractions relative to their kinetic energy

questions.ai_explanation: In a dilute gas, intermolecular attractions are weak compared with molecular kinetic energy. The molecules move freely and do not maintain the regular fixed arrangement found in a crystal.
questions.explanation: In a dilute gas, intermolecular attractions are weak compared with molecular kinetic energy. The molecules move freely and do not maintain the regular fixed arrangement found in a crystal.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The symmetry of an s orbital is
questions.ai_explanation: An s orbital has spherical symmetry: its probability density at a given distance from the nucleus is independent of direction.
questions.explanation: An s orbital has spherical symmetry: its probability density at a given distance from the nucleus is independent of direction.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which mixture contains a gas that can burn when supplied with air and ignited?
questions.ai_explanation: Hydrogen is combustible and can react with oxygen supplied by air. Neon is inert and acts as a diluent. The other listed mixtures contain no readily combustible gas.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: Which property difference explains why H–Cl has greater bond polarity than Cl–Cl?
questions.ai_explanation: Chlorine attracts bonding electrons more strongly than hydrogen, making H–Cl polar. In Cl–Cl the identical atoms share equally. The relevant property is electronegativity; molecular HCl is polar covalent.
questions.explanation: Chlorine attracts bonding electrons more strongly than hydrogen, making H–Cl polar. In Cl–Cl the identical atoms share equally. The relevant property is electronegativity; molecular HCl is polar covalent.

questions.question: A halogen atom gains one electron to form a halide ion with
questions.ai_explanation: A halogen atom has seven valence electrons. Gaining one electron forms a halide ion with a completed outer-shell octet.

questions.question: Extrapolating Charles’ law for an ideal gas gives zero volume at approximately

questions.question: The principal products when steam passes over red-hot carbon are
questions.ai_explanation: Steam reacts with red-hot carbon: C + H₂O(g) → CO + H₂. The mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen is called water gas.

questions.question: Aluminium hydroxide is used in dyeing as a

questions.question: Variable oxidation states of transition metals are closely associated with participation of their

options.B: d electrons as well as outer s electrons

questions.question: Which form of carbon is used to decolourise sugar solutions?

questions.question: In petroleum refining, the process that rearranges hydrocarbon structures to improve fuel quality is
questions.ai_explanation: Catalytic reforming rearranges hydrocarbon structures and can form branched, cyclic or aromatic molecules. It improves fuel properties such as octane rating; cracking chiefly breaks larger molecules into smaller ones.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: A common method of preparing an alloy from metals is

options.A: Cooling a molten mixture of the metals
options.B: Reducing a mixture of their metallic oxides

questions.ai_explanation: A common alloy-making method melts and mixes the constituent metals, then allows the mixture to solidify. This distributes the constituents through the resulting metallic material.

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.question: The main structural substance in cotton fibre is
questions.ai_explanation: Cotton fibres consist mainly of cellulose, a polymer of glucose units joined by β(1→4) glycosidic bonds. Starch is a different glucose polymer used chiefly for energy storage.
questions.explanation: Cotton fibres consist mainly of cellulose, a polymer of glucose units joined by β(1→4) glycosidic bonds. Starch is a different glucose polymer used chiefly for energy storage.

questions.question: The characteristic bleaching action of sulfur(IV) oxide is by

questions.question: The principal hydrocarbon constituent of natural gas is
